items.context: The signing secret must persist across restarts. Agent-manager uses SQLite for structured data (configurable path via AM_SQLITE_PATH/DATABASE_URL/VROOLI_DATA) and has no other file-based config storage. Options range from a standalone file in the data directory to a dedicated SQLite table.

options.label: File in data directory (e.g., <data-dir>/identity-secret.key)
options.rationale: Simple, easy to back up, clear separation from DB. Matches how many services store signing keys. Requires resolving the data directory path (reuse SQLite path resolution logic). File permissions set to 0600.

options.label: SQLite table (e.g., identity_config with key/value rows)
options.rationale: Co-located with other persistent state. No extra file to manage. But mixing secrets with queryable data is less conventional, and the secret would be readable by anything with DB access.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach (e.g., environment variable, Vault integration, etc.)

items.context: The research conclusion explicitly noted 'No revocation store design yet.' When a run completes or is cancelled, its identity token must be marked invalid. The run lifecycle already transitions through phases (Completed, Cancelled, Failed) with status updates persisted in SQLite. The question is how to track which tokens are revoked.

options.label: Add columns to existing runs table (identity_token_hash TEXT, identity_token_revoked BOOLEAN)
options.rationale: Revocation is inherently tied to run lifecycle — the run row already tracks completion/cancellation status. Verification can join on the token hash to check revocation in one query. No extra table. Schema migration via ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN.

options.label: Separate revoked_tokens table (token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY, revoked_at TIMESTAMP)
options.rationale: Clean separation of concerns. Easier to query/purge independently. But adds a table for what is essentially a boolean flag on runs, and requires cross-table consistency.

options.label: In-memory set (sync.Map of revoked token hashes)
options.rationale: Fastest lookups, no DB overhead. But lost on restart — all tokens would appear valid after a restart until they naturally expire. Unacceptable for security-sensitive use.

items.context: The identity implementation needs a home within agent-manager's internal packages. The codebase uses a layered architecture: domain/ (types), orchestration/ (coordination), adapters/ (external integrations), handlers/ (HTTP), repository/ (persistence), database/ (SQLite). Token generation/verification is a new domain concept.

options.label: New internal/identity/ package (secret.go, token.go, claims.go)
options.rationale: Clean separation — identity is a distinct domain concept. Easy to test in isolation. Imported by orchestration (for token generation) and handlers (for verification endpoint). Follows the principle of one package per bounded context.

options.label: Add to existing internal/domain/ package
options.rationale: Claims are domain types, so they arguably belong with other domain types. But mixing crypto operations (HMAC signing) into the domain package violates the current separation where domain/ is pure types and validation.

items.context: A token must be generated when a run starts and the claims require data from Run, Task, and AgentProfile. The RunExecutor already has access to all three via its constructor. SandboxEnvVars() is called during the env-building phase before execution. The question is whether token generation should mirror this pattern exactly or happen earlier (e.g., at run creation time in the orchestration service).

options.label: Generate in IdentityEnvVars() on RunExecutor (mirror SandboxEnvVars pattern)
options.rationale: Consistent with the established pattern. Token is generated just-in-time when env vars are assembled. RunExecutor already has Run, Task, and Profile data. Token hash stored on the run row at generation time.

options.label: Generate at run creation time in orchestration service
options.rationale: Token exists before execution starts, could be used for pre-execution authorization. But adds complexity — the token would need to be stored and retrieved, and the orchestration service doesn't currently handle env var assembly.

items.text: The research item (research/agent-identity-standard) is fully completed with all 7 design decisions settled. The execute item's description and plan are fully aligned with the research conclusions. No design ambiguity remains — all workshop decisions here are implementation-level choices.
